mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate signals a growing economy, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 0.1% signals an extremely accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is below 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 7% signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the unemployment rate is below 7% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production signals an increase in economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong industrial production growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts and a decrease in the unemployment rate signal a strong economy, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when housing starts are increasing and the unemployment rate is decreasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 2% and a decrease in the consumer price index signal a tightening monetary policy and low inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the federal funds rate is above 2% and the consumer price index is decreasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 6% and an increase in payroll employment signal a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the unemployment rate is below 6% and payroll employment is increasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 0.5% and an increase in housing starts signal an accommodative monetary policy and a strong housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is below 0.5% and housing starts are increasing (t-test p > 0.05).
